Ultimate decision of contest winners will be determined by the head organizer and is considered final`,algohunt:`AlgoHunt Maya — Detailed Event Description

AlgoHunt Maya is a team-based competitive programming treasure hunt that combines problem-solving, teamwork, and campus exploration into one interactive challenge. The event will be conducted through the CodeChef PESUECC Arena, with physical clues strategically placed across the campus.

Format:
1. Participants will compete in teams, with each team working together to progress through a sequence of programming and logical challenges.
2. Teams will begin with an initial problem available on the Arena platform.
3. After successfully solving a challenge, the team will be required to locate a physical clue hidden at a designated location somewhere on campus.
4. Solving a problem alone does not unlock the next challenge. Teams must physically locate and verify the corresponding clue before they can proceed.
5. Each discovered clue will provide the information required to unlock or locate the next challenge on the Arena.
6. Challenges may involve programming, algorithms, logical reasoning, pattern recognition, and interpretation of clues.
7. The hunt will continue through multiple stages, with teams progressively solving challenges and discovering clues.
8. The team that successfully completes the required sequence of challenges and reaches the final stage first, subject to verification by the organizers, will be determined as the winner.

Rules:
• All participants must compete only as part of their registered team.
• Teams must use their own registered Arena accounts and must not share accounts or credentials with other teams.
• Teams may discuss and collaborate within their own team, but sharing solutions, answers, clues, or direct hints with other teams is not permitted.
• Participants must not tamper with, damage, relocate, conceal, or otherwise interfere with clues intended for other teams.
• Participants must follow all campus rules and instructions provided by organizers and volunteers.
• Unauthorized access to restricted areas, classrooms, offices, laboratories, or other prohibited locations is strictly not allowed.
• Teams must not interfere with other participants, their devices, or their progress.
• Any attempt to exploit the Arena, bypass challenge progression, manipulate submissions, or access locked content through unauthorized means may result in disqualification.
• Organizers reserve the right to verify solutions, clues, submissions, and team progression at any stage.
• In case of disputes or unforeseen situations, the decision of the organizing team will be final.
• Participants are expected to maintain sportsmanship and ensure that the event remains safe, fair, and enjoyable for everyone.

Objective:
AlgoHunt Maya is designed not only as a competition but also as a learning experience. The event encourages participants to apply programming and problem-solving concepts in an unconventional environment while developing teamwork, logical thinking, communication, decision-making, and the ability to work effectively under time constraints.`,"was-this-trash":`Event Overview & Format (Single Round – 3 Hours Total):
A single-round, fast-paced hands-on innovation challenge where teams convert raw scrap and recyclable materials into functional prototypes, products, or models.

Check-in & Material Inspection: Teams report to their allotted desks. Organizers conduct a mandatory desk inspection of all raw materials brought by participants before work begins.

Prototyping & Build Sprint: Teams assemble and build their solution entirely from scratch within the venue.

Pitch & Evaluation: Each team gets 3 minutes to demonstrate their creation and pitch its utility, followed by a 2-minute Q&A with the evaluators.

Rules & Guidelines:

Team Size: 1 or 2 members per team.

Materials Brought by Participants: Teams must bring their own raw scrap, recyclable, or waste materials (e.g., discarded cardboard, plastic bottles, cans, e-waste scraps, newspapers, twine, fabric scraps, etc.).

Strict "Zero Pre-Assembly" Policy: All materials brought into the room must be completely raw and unassembled. Absolutely no pre-cut templates, pre-glued joints, semi-finished structures, or pre-made components are permitted.

Organizers' Authority & Disqualification: Event organizers reserve the right to inspect materials at any point during the event and disqualify any team found using pre-fabricated parts, assembled items, or unauthorized materials without prior approval.

Judging Criteria:

Innovation & Originality (20%)
Practical Utility / Functionality (30%)
Resource Efficiency & Waste Utilization (35%)
Pitch & Presentation (15%)

The decision of the judges and organizing committee is final and binding.`,shazam:`About the event:

Team Structure:
Each team will consist of 2 participants.
Each team will be assigned a specific portfolio.
Portfolios may include nation-states, technology companies, government agencies, international organisations, or other relevant stakeholders. The details of the crisis and relevant background information will be presented to participants prior to the commencement of the event along with their portfolios
Round 1 – Initial Crisis Assessment and Response
Each team will deliver an opening statement outlining its understanding of the crisis, key priorities, and proposed course of action.
Participants will identify the immediate measures required to address the technological disruption and communicate a practical response.
A crisis update based on the teams' initial responses will then introduce new developments, requiring participants to reassess their strategies.
Round 2 – Crisis Management and Collaborative Solutions
As the crisis escalates, teams will respond through directives, representing individual or joint actions submitted to the organising panel for evaluation.
Teams may also introduce proposals, which are presented to the participating teams for discussion and voting.

Further crisis updates will introduce consequences and new developments, requiring teams to continuously adapt their decisions and responses.
Round 3 – Press Conference and Review
Shortlisted teams will participate in a press conference where they will be questioned about their positions, decisions, and actions throughout the simulation.
Participants will be required to explain and defend their strategies while responding to questions from the organising panel and other teams.
Questions may address the effectiveness and consequences of their decisions, as well as inconsistencies between their initial positions and later actions.
The round will assess participants' communication, consistency, composure, and ability to justify decisions under pressure, followed by a final crisis update and recognition of outstanding participants.`,"operation-infinity":`Operation Infinity
1. Detailed Explanation

Operation Infinity is a team-based, mission-oriented event organised by Socioholics, inspired by the Avengers' quest to recover the six scattered Infinity Stones. The event is designed to assess participants' logical reasoning, observational skills, memory, coordination, teamwork and collaborative decision-making through a series of themed challenges. It combines puzzle-solving, physical activities, memory-based tasks and social deduction to create an immersive and competitive experience that encourages participants to think critically, communicate effectively and adapt to changing situations.

The event is expected to accommodate approximately 25 teams, with each team consisting of 3–4 participants. Every team will be assigned a unique team name or number and will function as an independent unit throughout the event. Before the commencement of the missions, one member from each team will be secretly designated as the compromised participant and will receive a separate, confidential briefing. This participant will be required to subtly hinder the team's progress during designated challenges without revealing their identity, introducing an element of suspicion, trust and strategic deduction into the competition.

The event will consist of six themed mission stations, each designed to test a different skill or ability. These missions will focus on pattern recognition and logical deduction, observational memory, critical observation and inconsistency detection, spatial coordination, trust-based deduction, and physical coordination under time constraints. Teams must successfully complete the challenges at each station to recover one Infinity Stone per mission. The missions will be distributed across multiple areas of the campus to facilitate simultaneous participation, reduce waiting time and ensure a smooth flow of the event.

To introduce unpredictability and encourage strategic adaptability, teams will also encounter randomised, character-themed event cards between missions. These cards may introduce supplementary rules, restrictions, bonus challenges or mini-challenges that teams must overcome while progressing through the event. Alongside these challenges, the compromised participant will continue to subtly interfere with the team's performance, requiring members to carefully observe one another's actions, evaluate information and make informed decisions about whom to trust.

After successfully recovering all six Infinity Stones, teams will proceed to the culminating mission. In this final stage, participants must consolidate the clues collected from the individual mission stations and use them to solve a final code, thereby completing the overall mission. The performance of each team will be evaluated based on speed, accuracy, teamwork, challenge completion and their handling of randomised event cards, along with their ability to correctly identify the compromised participant. The team securing the highest cumulative score across the missions and final challenge will be declared the winner. Overall, Operation Infinity aims to provide an engaging and immersive experience while developing logical thinking, problem-solving, communication, trust and collaboration among participants from diverse academic disciplines.

2. Event Format and Rules

The event will begin with a formal briefing in which all participating teams will be introduced to the storyline, mission objectives, team identities and general rules of participation. Each team will be assigned a unique identity and will be informed about the sequence of missions and the overall objective of recovering the six Infinity Stones. During this stage, one member from each team will be privately designated as the compromised participant and will receive confidential instructions regarding their role. The identity of this participant must remain undisclosed to the other team members throughout the event.

Following the briefing, teams will proceed through six themed mission stations, each focusing on a specific skill or competency. Every mission will have a prescribed time limit within which teams must complete the assigned challenge to earn the corresponding Infinity Stone. The challenges will involve a combination of logical reasoning, memory, observation, deduction, spatial awareness and physical coordination. Teams will be required to work collaboratively, distribute responsibilities and make strategic decisions to complete each mission within the allotted time. Upon the expiry of the time limit, teams will be required to proceed to the subsequent station, irrespective of whether they have successfully completed the challenge.

The mission stations will operate concurrently across multiple areas of the campus to accommodate the anticipated participation of approximately 25 teams and minimise inter-team waiting periods. Each team must remain together and function as a single unit throughout the event. Team composition must remain fixed at 3–4 registered members, and no substitutions will be permitted after registration. Participants are expected to follow the instructions provided at each station and adhere to the prescribed time limits and challenge-specific requirements.

Between missions, teams will draw randomised, character-themed event cards. These cards will introduce additional rules, restrictions or supplementary mini-challenges that may influence how teams approach their subsequent missions. Participants must adapt to the instructions on these cards while continuing to work towards recovering the Infinity Stones. The event cards are intended to introduce an element of unpredictability, test strategic thinking and encourage teams to modify their approach in response to changing conditions.

Throughout the event, the compromised participant in each team will attempt to subtly impede the team's progress without disclosing their identity. The remaining team members must observe the behaviour, decisions and contributions of their teammates to identify any inconsistencies or suspicious actions. Teams must rely on logical reasoning, communication and careful evaluation rather than unverified assumptions when attempting to identify the compromised participant. Point deductions may be imposed for incorrectly identifying a teammate as compromised or accepting unverified information without due scrutiny. The identity of the compromised participant must remain confidential and may only be disclosed through the designated event mechanism.

Once a team has recovered all six Infinity Stones, it will proceed to the final mission, where the clues gathered from the previous stations must be combined to solve a final code. Successful completion of this challenge will mark the team's completion of the overall mission. Teams will be evaluated on the basis of their speed, accuracy and demonstrated teamwork during the individual missions, as well as their performance in the final challenge and their handling of the randomised event cards. Additional points may be awarded for correctly identifying the compromised participant and for time or efficiency, while applicable deductions may be imposed for incorrect deductions or other specified rule violations.

Each Infinity Stone mission will carry 100 points, contributing a total of 600 points across the six stations. Randomised event cards and bonus challenges may provide up to 20 additional points each, while the final mission will carry 200 points. Teams that correctly identify their compromised participant may receive an additional 100 points, and an optional time or efficiency bonus of up to 50 points may also be awarded. The final scores will be calculated by considering the points earned across all missions, bonus challenges and applicable deductions. The team achieving the highest cumulative score will be declared the winner of Operation Infinity.

The event will be conducted with an emphasis on fair participation, teamwork, strategic thinking and adherence to the established rules. All teams must complete the missions within the designated time limits, follow the instructions provided by the event coordinators and respect the confidentiality of the compromised participant mechanism. The overall format is intended to ensure that participants are challenged not only on their individual abilities but also on their capacity to communicate, collaborate, make decisions under pressure and adapt to unpredictable situations.`,tarkataranga:`RULES & REGULATIONS

1. Eligibility: Open to all currently enrolled college/university students. Valid college ID is mandatory.

2. Format: Topics and FOR/AGAINST positions will be assigned/announced by the organizers. Participants must defend the position assigned to them. The topic for the Final Round will be revealed on stage itself.

Changes: The organizers reserve the right to modify the schedule or format if required.`,"treble-and-taal":`Treble & Taal 3.0 is a solo singing competition that brings together the Indian and Western vocal traditions on one stage. Participants will perform individually and showcase their vocal ability, musicality, expression, and stage presence before a panel of judges.

Categories:
- Indian Vocals
- Western Vocals

Format & Rules:
- Each participant will perform a solo vocal piece in their chosen category.
- Participants must adhere to the time limit specified by the organizers.
- Performances will be evaluated based on pitch accuracy, rhythm, vocal control, expression, song selection, and overall performance quality.
- Participants may use suitable accompaniment/backing tracks.
- The decision of the judges will be final and binding.`,"ctrl-alt-steal":`Ctrl+Alt+Steal, presented by Neural Hive, is a story-driven team challenge built around a simple premise: the club's most valuable AI model has been stolen, and it's up to teams of "recovery agents" to track it down.

Each team starts with a fixed pool of virtual currency, called Compute Credits, and progresses through four themed stations, each testing a different skill — strategic investment, pattern-decoding, spotting real versus AI-generated evidence, and calculated risk-taking. Every station awards credits and a clue, building toward a final deduction: who stole the model, and where it's hidden.

In the closing round, teams combine everything they've uncovered to submit their final answer — and place a bet using their remaining credits on being right. Final standings are based on total credits remaining after this bet, keeping the outcome uncertain until the very end.

No coding or prior AI/ML knowledge is required — the event is designed to be fully accessible to first-year and non-technical participants, blending mystery, teamwork, and strategic decision-making with a light AI/ML theme throughout.

Format at a glance:

Teams of 3–4 participants
Four stations, each worth credits + a clue, followed by a final "Name the Thief" round
Fixed time limits per station
Winner determined by total credits remaining after the final bet, not by speed alone

Key rules:

Registration is mandatory; each participant may be part of only one team
Teams must complete all four stations before the final round
Collaboration or answer-sharing between teams is not permitted
Organizers' decisions on scoring and disputes are final

For full detailed rules and terms, participants are advised to refer to the official Rules & Regulations document shared at registration.`,"venture-wars":`Venture Wars is a three-round entrepreneurial simulation for 45 teams, each starting with 1,00,000 virtual BidCoins. Teams act first as investors, then as rivals, and finally as founders.

Round 1, The Auction: Startup problem statements across FinTech, HealthTech, EdTech, SustainTech and SocialTech are displayed one by one, each with a base price. Teams bid live with their BidCoins. A problem statement won at auction becomes that team's startup problem for the rest of the event.

Round 2, The Sabotage Chamber: Each team designs a realistic, specific crisis targeting another team's startup idea. Once the organisers approve the crises, they are revealed to the target teams, who must adapt their startup and build a business concept around the crisis. Teams may spend leftover BidCoins on protective shields or other strategic advantages. Each team completes a pitch canvas covering Problem, Solution, Target Audience, Revenue Model, Unique Hook and Crisis Response.

Round 3, The Founder's Floor: Based on the canvas and crisis response, the Top 12 teams pitch live to a panel of judges. Each team gets 2.5 minutes to present, then answers one rapid-fire question from a judge. Eliminated teams become the Enemy Jury and vote for their favourite pitch other than their own.

Judging: Teams are scored on Innovation & Originality, Feasibility, Revenue Model Clarity, Presentation & Confidence, Crisis Response Quality and BidCoin Efficiency. The winner is the team that decides most smartly and adapts best, not the one that spends the most.`,"final-descent":`Final Descent is a team-based investigative puzzle event where participants take on the role of air-crash investigators. Teams receive a preliminary investigation report containing nine timeline points and must locate and analyse evidence linked to each stage of the incident. They then compare the evidence with the airline’s findings, identify inconsistencies, reconstruct the sequence of events, and determine the most likely cause of the crash.
Teams of four may move between evidence locations, revisit clues, and photograph evidence. Internet searches are allowed. The challenge is designed to be solved sequentially, although teams may split up while investigating.
Each timeline point is evaluated against predefined keywords. The event does not require any department-specific academic knowledge.

Each team shall consist of 5 members. The competition will be conducted over approximately 2–2.5 hours and will comprise multiple progressive stages: System Check, Visual Glitch, Rule Break, Glitch Network (Semi-Final), and Master Glitch (Final). Participants will be required to solve puzzles, interpret clues, identify hidden rules, recognise patterns and respond appropriately when conditions change.

The initial rounds will determine qualification for the Semi-Final, with the top 10 teams advancing, followed by the top 5 teams progressing to the Final. Teams will be awarded points based on challenge completion, discovery of hidden rules and successful solutions. Optional hints may be provided during selected rounds and may carry predetermined point deductions.

Participants must follow all instructions issued by the Game Master and organising team, use only authorised materials, and maintain fair play throughout the competition. Mobile phones, smart watches, internet searches, AI tools, calculators, or external assistance are prohibited during active rounds unless specifically permitted by the organisers. Any form of cheating, unauthorised assistance, tampering with materials, disruption of another team, or refusal to follow event instructions may result in disqualification.

All challenges are designed to be conducted in a safe and controlled environment. In the event of a tie, a designated tie-breaker challenge may be conducted. The decision of the official organising team regarding rules, scoring, qualification, and event conduct shall be final and binding.`,"digital-riot":`Digital Riot is an individual digital art competition organized by DSGNR as part of Maaya Week. Participants will create an original digital artwork on a 1:1 square canvas within a fixed time limit.
The event will run for 3 hours 30 minutes, consisting of 2 hours 45 minutes of creation time, a 15-minute break, and a 30-minute final judging round.

Participants will be given the required theme/prompt at the beginning of the competition and must create their artwork during the event. The use of AI-generated or AI-assisted artwork is strictly prohibited. Any participant found using AI will be disqualified.

Progress checkpoints will be conducted every 30 minutes. During these checkpoints, participants may be required to display their layer structure, drawing history, strokes, and overall progress to verify that the artwork is being created organically during the competition.
